transcript:
Meeting header: Northpoint Labs x Redwood Inference - throughput & hosting probe
Date/Time: 2027-09-01 16:00 PT | Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Li (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Evan Cortez (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Northpoint CTO), Leena Park (SRE Lead), Omar Ruiz (Product PM), Sofia Mendes (Security)

Summary:
Quick discovery to decide hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC) driven by p95 latency targets for streaming chat and batch token generation. Focus on concurrency, burst windows (token floods), steady-state throughput, and a short benchmark plan. Security and residency constraints are discussed (SOC2, SSO, KMS).

Topics:
- Current p95 targets: 300ms for short-chat messages, 1.2s for 512-token generations (target)
- Expected concurrency: 250 concurrent chat sessions at peak, 1k short-lived bursts/day
- Streaming vs non-streaming behavior and token/sec profiling
- Hosted vs Dedicated cost tradeoffs, fallback strategies and quantization considerations
- Security: audit logs, SSO/SAML, BYOK/KMS, data residency in us-west-2

Action items (captured verbally): Marcus to share cost matrix; Priya to prepare benchmark plan; Leena to send token distribution sample.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marcus Li: Hey all, thanks for making time. I'll kick us off — quick agenda: understand p95 goals, concurrency, and whether you'll go hosted or want dedicated slices. Priya will cover benchmark approach.
[00:12] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks Marcus. Quick context — Northpoint's building a conversational assistant inside our lab portal. Our big worry is p95 tail for short-turn responses, we need it under 300ms in the UI, else clinicians complain. For longer generations we can accept up to ~1.2 seconds for about 512 tokens.
[00:29] Leena Park: Right, we see a mix — most requests are short, 8-40 tokens, but we get spikes where users kick off long reports, those are the token floods. Our current system is on-prem TPU cluster but it's expensive and opaque.
[00:45] Priya Shah: Got it — so two profiles: streaming short bursts (chat) and batch-ish long gens. Can you confirm peak concurrency?
[00:52] Omar Ruiz: We model 250 concurrent chat sessions at peak, with about 1k burst events (the long report jobs) distributed through the day. The bursts can overlap during morning shift.
[01:05] Evan Cortez: A couple clarifying q's: are your p95 numbers measured end-to-end including network and UI render, or just inference?
[01:11] Daniel Ortiz: End-to-end right now, but for our decision we want to understand inference-only p95. We can subtract ~40-60ms for UI and network in our region.
[01:23] Marcus Li: Perfect. For Redwood we usually present both: model inference p95 and end-to-end modeled numbers. For hosted we can show regional latencies; dedicated gives better predictability at scale.
[01:35] Leena Park: Security is also a gating factor — must be SOC2, SSO via SAML, and we prefer BYOK KMS with keys in our AWS account. Also data residency in us-west-2.
[01:48] Sofia Mendes: If it's private deployment, we need audit logs retained for 1 year and ability to export to our SIEM.
[01:55] Marcus Li: Noted — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC deployments; audit export is supported. We'll attach the security pack.
[02:03] Daniel Ortiz: Great. Cost will push us — hosted is simpler but we're worried about noisy neighbors making p95 go bad. How do you mitigate that?
[02:13] Priya Shah: We have routing policies and dedicated capacity. For hosted we do smart routing and model variants, plus automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants if latency spikes. But that can affect quality. For strict p95 we usually recommend Dedicated.
[02:26] Leena Park: How strict is the fallback? If a model is quantized down, how do you detect quality regressions?
[02:31] Priya Shah: We tie regressions to eval sets and prompt tests. For production we can attach a canary and automatic rollback — Redwood Optimize flags quality drift. But we normally include a grace policy so production isn't silently changed without alerting the team.
[02:47] Omar Ruiz: Let's talk numbers: can Dedicated hit 300ms p95 for shallow chat at 256 token windows with 250 concurrent?
[02:54] Evan Cortez: Roughly — depends on model and hardware. On Ampere A100s or similar with optimized kernels and batching disabled for low-latency paths, we can get ~120–200ms inference p95 for small models. For larger models we'd shift to model variants. But concurrency affects available batch slots; dedicated capacity lets you reserve throughput.
[03:15] Daniel Ortiz: And for streaming, token/sec matters more than single-token latency. We need consistent streaming throughput so chat tokens arrive smoothly — target about 30 tokens/sec sustained per chat session during active generation? That sounds high.
[03:27] Priya Shah: 30 tokens/sec sustained per session is high; most chats average 8–12 tokens/sec depending on model chunking. Are you seeing 30 in logs?
[03:33] Leena Park: In peak busy demos yes. Our demo rig intentionally pushes 20–25 tokens/sec. But we can profile.
[03:39] Marcus Li: For the benchmark, we'll run three scenarios: 1) steady-state chat (250 concurrent, 8–40 tokens, streaming) 2) burst overlay (250 concurrent plus 100 overlapping 512-token jobs) 3) isolated long gens (single-job p95 profiling). We'll capture model-only p95 and simulated end-to-end.
[03:58] Daniel Ortiz: Sounds good. How long does a benchmark window need to be?
[04:02] Priya Shah: For steady-state, 15–30 minutes with warm-up to capture KV cache behavior. For bursts, we prefer a 2-hour window to schedule overlapping jobs. We'll provide a reproducible load script.
[04:13] Leena Park: Are you using KV caching or prefix cache in Hosted? We want to reduce cost by caching common prompts.
[04:18] Evan Cortez: Yes — Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching which helps reduce per-token work for repeated context. We'll ask for a sample request distribution so we can configure cache hits.
[04:29] Omar Ruiz: Another gating item: can we run the benchmark in our VPC or at least from a peered network to measure real network hops?
[04:36] Priya Shah: For Dedicated and Private we can deploy in your VPC (private control plane). For hosted we can provide a test endpoint in us-west-2; peering is possible on enterprise plans. We'll note options in the follow-up.
[04:49] Daniel Ortiz: About quantization — we saw a 2x throughput gain on a quantized 4-bit variant elsewhere but the hallucination rate went up. What's Redwood's guidance?
[04:59] Marcus Li: Quantization helps cost and throughput but must be validated against your eval prompts. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles by workload, but we recommend a canary and A/B. For clinical content I'd be cautious on aggressive quantization.
[05:12] Sofia Mendes: For compliance, we need a reproducible audit trail in case of a question — can Redwood provide per-request metadata with model version and quantization used?
[05:20] Priya Shah: Yes, each token request includes model version, runtime flags, and tracing IDs. That metadata can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[05:28] Leena Park: What about autoscaling? During burst windows we need immediate capacity. Dedicated autoscale with burst credits — how predictable is that?
[05:36] Evan Cortez: Dedicated has predictable autoscaling with warm and cold pools; you can configure burst capacity. SLA covers fallbacks; if capacity is exhausted we can route to a lower-cost variant or fallback region depending on policy.
[05:49] Marcus Li: We'll include an example burst policy in the follow-up doc.
[05:54] Omar Ruiz: One last technical: tokenization differences — we need to ensure token counts are consistent across our telemetry and your bench harness. Any gotchas?
[06:02] Priya Shah: We'll share the tokenizer version we use for the benchmark and map it to your telemetry. Sometimes token counts differ by a token or two due to special tokens; we'll normalize in the scripts.
[06:12] Daniel Ortiz: Ok recap from our side: we want a hosted POC to start baseline, but if the p95 can't be guaranteed we'll pivot to Dedicated. Must have BYOK and audit export; trial perf run next week ideally.
[06:24] Marcus Li: Recap from Redwood: we'll share hosted vs dedicated cost matrix, a 3-scenario benchmark plan, and a security pack. Priya will book the 2-hour burst window.
[06:33] Leena Park: And we'll send sample traces and p95 logs and a list of the most common prompts.
[06:39] Sofia Mendes: I'll also request SOC2 certificate and KMS onboarding doc.
[06:44] Marcus Li: Great. Any other questions?
[06:47] Daniel Ortiz: Quick competitive note — we ran a benchmark with GigaAI and saw jitter under load; curious if Redwood can provide jitter graphs in the report.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Absolutely, we'll include jitter (p50/p90/p95/p99) and token throughput curves and annotate where fallbacks occurred.
[07:04] Evan Cortez: We'll also include guidance on model selection and a suggested quantization profile for the three scenarios.
[07:13] Omar Ruiz: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:16] Marcus Li: Thanks — we'll drop next steps and schedule links in the calendar invite.

End of call.

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-attributed speaker label around 03:00-04:00, small stutters and filler words preserved. Some product names transcribed as Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Priviate in quick talk portions.
